challenges.title: Saudi Labor Law, Ramadan and the 12-Hour Limit

items.title: Standard Hours & the 6-Day Limit
items.text: Standard working time is capped at 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week (Art. 98). Since the 2025 reform, an additional rule applies: no more than 6 consecutive working days without a full rest day.

items.title: Ramadan: Shorter Working Hours
items.text: For Muslim staff, actual working hours mandatorily drop during شهر رمضان (Shahr Ramadan) to a maximum of 6 hours per day or 36 hours per week — recalculated every year for exactly this group.

items.title: 12-Hour Presence Limit (Art. 101)
items.text: No employee may remain at the workplace (التواجد في مكان العمل) for more than 12 hours — including breaks, prayer and meal times. In addition, after a maximum of 5 hours of continuous work, a break of at least 30 minutes is mandatory.

rulesCalendar.title: A calendar that follows the moon
rulesCalendar.text: In Saudi Arabia, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development decrees all four official public holidays centrally — uniformly across the whole Kingdom, with no provincial or municipal level like in Europe. The real challenge lies elsewhere: the two religious holidays, whose exact date is only confirmed at short notice by moon sighting.

items.title: Uniform nationwide, no regional level
items.text: Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, National Day on September 23 and Founding Day on February 22 apply unchanged across the whole Kingdom — for the public and private sector alike, with no cantonal or municipal exceptions.

items.title: Mix calendars
items.text: A business based in Riyadh or Dhahran with partners in the Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain or Oman needs several country calendars running at once — moon sightings occasionally differ by a day between Gulf states, as they did between Saudi Arabia and Oman in 2023.

items.title: Binding or purely informational
items.text: For each calendar, you decide whether a holiday affects hours & premiums — or simply appears as a reminder.

rulesCalendar.imageAlt: Holiday rules in Klacks: public holidays of the United Kingdom, each with its country and region
rulesCalendar.imageCaption: Real rules from Klacks: every holiday rule carries a country and a region, and the list can be filtered by both — freely extensible.

solutions.title: How Klacks Takes the Load Off Businesses in Saudi Arabia
solutions.subtitle: From automatic 12-hour monitoring to your own infrastructure — it all fits together.

items.title: Standard Hours & 6-Day Limit Monitored
items.text: Klacks knows the 8h/48h limit (Art. 98) and the new rule of max. 6 consecutive working days without a rest day — Klacks monitors both limits live and warns in time before either is exceeded. On request, Klacks hard-blocks the excess in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning.

items.title: Ramadan Hours Configurable as a Rule
items.text: For Muslim staff, the reduced 6h/36h limit (Art. 98) for Ramadan can be configured as a separate rule — Klacks checks the schedule against it and warns when it is exceeded.

items.title: 12-Hour Limit Monitored Live (Art. 101)
items.text: Klacks checks the configured 12-hour daily limit live and warns immediately if a person would be scheduled for longer on a single day. On request, Klacks hard-blocks such violations in automatic planning (block mode, configurable per rule type); with manual planning it stays at a warning.

items.title: Overtime Premium under Art. 107 as Time Credit
items.text: The statutory premium of 50% on the base wage (effectively 150%) can be stored as a time premium; Klacks credits the premium hours, and your payroll system calculates the money amount — since the 2025 reform, optionally also as paid time off in lieu.

items.title: Nitaqat Saudization Stays in Your Payroll System
items.text: Klacks does not map Nitaqat classification and does not calculate salaries — whether the GOSI salary threshold for the full quota unit (1.0 from SAR 4,000, 0.5 for SAR 3,000 to 3,999) is met is checked by your payroll system. Klacks provides the hours worked for this as a file export.

items.title: Installed on Your Premises: Data Storage on Your Servers in Saudi Arabia
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure, and you choose the AI model. Sensitive personnel and scheduling data (البيانات الشخصية الحساسة) is stored physically on your servers within KSA — with a locally hosted AI model, no AI request goes to an external AI provider; transfers are governed by the PDPL and SDAIA, and the legal assessment remains with you.

items.title: Klacksy: Rule-Based, No Black Box
items.text: The built-in AI assistant Klacksy understands instructions in everyday language and controls Klacks; the rule-based planning engine calculates the plan — traceable through defined rules, not an opaque AI decision.

items.title: Test Plan Changes Risk-Free
items.text: Before a plan change goes live, you can run it through as an isolated copy — the 12-hour daily limit (Art. 101) and premiums are calculated live exactly as in the real plan. Only once everything checks out do you apply the variant; until then, your live schedule stays untouched. This lets you prepare a suitable scenario in advance for foreseeable situations — such as a staff member calling in sick or a sudden spike in orders — so you're ready to act immediately when it matters, instead of improvising under time pressure. There's no artificial limit on the number of scenarios — create as many as your planning needs.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: The Built-In Assistant for Your Team
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn’t a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it’s embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shift times via chat or check availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy makes transparent suggestions — never a black-box decision. For businesses with strict requirements for meeting PDPL/SDAIA, the AI model can also be hosted locally in Saudi Arabia.
